title: What a CBC measures
text: A complete blood count measures the number and size of blood cells. It commonly includes red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and MCV. It is one part of a clinical assessment.

title: Why results need context
text: A laboratory result alone does not give a full picture of health. A clinician combines results with symptoms, medical history, examination and other tests. Do not use one abnormal CBC number to decide a diagnosis or treatment.

title: Use the range on the report
text: Reference ranges can differ between laboratories and groups of people. Compare a value with the reference interval printed next to that value on the same report. A value just outside a range does not by itself identify a disease.

title: Hemoglobin basics
text: Hemoglobin is the oxygen carrying protein in red blood cells. A hemoglobin test measures how much is in the blood. A clinician may review a low or high result with other CBC values and the person's history.

title: Low hemoglobin
text: Hemoglobin below the report's interval is a low reading. It does not identify the reason. A clinician can interpret it alongside symptoms, red cell measures and any further tests they consider appropriate.

title: High hemoglobin
text: Hemoglobin above the report's interval is a high reading. The number alone cannot explain the cause; review the full report and health history with a clinician.

title: White blood cell count
text: White blood cells are part of the immune system. A WBC test counts them in a blood sample. A total WBC count is different from a differential count, which breaks white cells into types.

title: WBC outside the range
topic: wbc white blood cells high low
text: A WBC value outside the printed interval can occur for several reasons. The count alone does not establish infection, its cause, or the need for medication. A clinician may consider symptoms and a differential count.

title: Red blood cell count
text: A red blood cell count is the number of red blood cells in a blood sample. Red cells carry hemoglobin. Clinicians often read the count together with hemoglobin, hematocrit and red cell indices.

title: Hematocrit
text: Hematocrit is the proportion of blood volume made up of red blood cells. It is a CBC measure and is interpreted together with other blood measurements and clinical context.

title: MCV
text: Mean corpuscular volume measures the average size of red blood cells. It can help a clinician interpret other red cell findings but does not establish a diagnosis on its own.

title: Low MCV
topic: mcv mean corpuscular volume low small red cells
text: An MCV below the report's interval means the average red blood cell size is smaller than that interval. It is a clue for clinical review, not proof of a particular cause. Hemoglobin and other results matter too.

title: High MCV
topic: mcv mean corpuscular volume high large red cells
text: An MCV above the report's interval means the average red blood cell size is larger than that interval. A clinician interprets it with the rest of the CBC and medical history.

title: Platelets
text: Platelets are cell fragments that help blood clot. A platelet count is part of a CBC. The result alone does not determine bleeding risk for an individual.

title: Platelets outside the range
text: A platelet result above or below the report's interval needs clinical interpretation. Symptoms, other test results and medical history affect what it means; do not infer a cause from the count alone.

title: Missing reference interval
text: If a report does not show a reference interval for a value, this app can repeat the value but cannot label it high or low. Ask the laboratory or clinician for the applicable range.

title: Questions for a clinician
text: Useful questions include which findings need follow up, whether any repeat test is needed, how symptoms change interpretation, and when to seek care. The app cannot prescribe next steps for an individual.

title: Limits of a CBC
text: A CBC can help a clinician evaluate overall health or monitor conditions, but a CBC is not a standalone diagnosis. A normal CBC does not rule out every health problem.

title: Why MCV may be low
topic: mcv low possible causes iron deficiency thalassemia
text: A low MCV can be seen with iron deficiency anemia or inherited conditions such as thalassemia. MCV alone cannot distinguish these possibilities or diagnose a disease; a clinician uses other results and medical history.

title: Why hemoglobin may be low
topic: hemoglobin hb low possible causes iron deficiency blood loss
text: Low hemoglobin can have different explanations, including iron deficiency, blood loss, or other types of anemia. A hemoglobin result alone does not identify the cause. A clinician considers symptoms and other blood tests.

title: Why WBC may be high
topic: wbc high possible causes infection inflammation stress medicine
text: A high white blood cell count can occur with infection, inflammation, stress, smoking, or a reaction to medicine, among other reasons. The total WBC count cannot confirm which explanation applies; symptoms and sometimes a differential count provide context.

title: Why platelets may be low
topic: platelets low possible causes viral infection medicines
text: A low platelet count can have different causes, including viral infections, medicines, or other conditions. The number alone cannot identify the cause or determine an individual's bleeding risk. A clinician reviews symptoms and other results.
